💡 Key Takeaways
  • The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.
  • Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.
  • Industry observers note that xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

Industry observers note that xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

"Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.".

Industry observers note that performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones.".

Industry observers note that from their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

Industry observers note that streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

Latency also looks to be the big winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

"Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.".

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

Of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Industry observers note that have you tried Xbox Cloud streaming GTA VI? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

GTA 6 has notably debuted without a PC release, landing on PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X|S only – a debacle that has, of course, led to fans attempting to get the Grand Theft Auto entry running on computers.

Industry observers note that there are various "projects," so to speak, attempting to tackle an unofficial PC port – but one in particular made rounds recently after Rockstar allegedly took its Discord server down and prompted its lead – an anonymous 15-year-old (as per their own words) – to say "goodbye," noting that "managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." Well, they're back… and so is their project, Leonida. And, according to a fresh post on Twitter from "NotRexed," the Leonida lead, they'll provide more information on their supposed GTA 6 PC port in the coming days. "Leonida is NOT dead," they write. "I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I'll have some stuff to show all of you soon." They follow up on this with a response stating that Leonida should feature "native Linux support," with "more on that later.".

According to recent reports, obviously, it's difficult to verify anything they say, seeing as this is a (very) unofficial port, should it be happening at all. Rockstar itself hasn't actually spoken on the matter publicly. It all stemmed from notorious GTA 6 leaker "Cyberleek," who recently uploaded an executable file and the Xbox build of the game online. Shortly after, fans like NotRexed picked it up and began working toward a PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sources indicate that I'm not so sure what'll happen from here, but I am personally left wondering when Rockstar will announce an official PC release of the game. It's no small launch, after all, smashing records as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and proving "the biggest launch in PlayStation history" (with Sony reporting "more than 39 million unique players" playing on the PS5 alone). Imagine how those numbers could grow….

Dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have unveiled Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.

Symphony of War II: Dominion Announcement Trailer | Strategy RPG Watch on YouTube.

Sources indicate that dominion's premise mirrors its predecessor in setting a band of heroes from a wide variety of classes, with units ranging from heavy knights and light archers to cannon-lighting artillery and even dragons the size of large dogs; I do have to wonder if an actual hooded horse is one of the units. Over 100 different classes are available, with the core of the game being swapping out these units to create the most effective squads of units for each turn-based battle. As before, it's not just a matter of recruiting soldiers and never thinking about them again until their turn arrives; a cared for army is a strong army (Sun Tzu mentioned that, probably), and nurturing your army with fresh gear, individual perks and specialisation to make the squad work not only on their own, but as a collective.

It has been revealed that phil Hamilton, founder of Dancing Dragon Games, elaborated that "With Symphony of War: Dominion, we’re building on what players loved about the first game while taking the series in a direction we’ve wanted to explore for years. We’re delivering a deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG without sacrificing the feel and flow that made the original special." Symphony of War II: Dominion releases sometime next year, so for now, get thinking about how you'll best take care of your squads. To paraphrase Sun Tzu again, keeping them fed is always a good start.

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player says they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 stated they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

It has been revealed that "Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found.".

In a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety says that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and indicates Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

In a recent development, DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt.

Industry observers note that crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Legendary BBC football commentator John "Motty" Motson, who died in 2023 at age 77, is being added to EA Sports FC 27 through "a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself." The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.

It has been revealed that motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames, but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series says "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "new AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.

It has been revealed that "My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred stated. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole fresh set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.".

Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." The BBC report also notes that EA paid the Motson family an undisclosed sum for the right to use John's voice.

According to recent reports, not everyone shares Fred Motson's enthusiasm. While plenty in the EA Sports FC subreddit are excited by the prospect, others refer to it with terms like "shameful," "disrespectful," "gross," and "bloody dark.".

Recent findings suggest that "What a bleak fucking world we live in," redditor forameus2 wrote. "You can't even escape in death.".

"Honestly, it's kind of gross for me," jlo1989 added.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"If anyone from my family uses AI to resurrect me in some perverse way like this, I'll fucking haunt them," niallmul97 wrote.

Peter Caulfield of the Save Our Voices Now campaign against unauthorized voice cloning told the BBC he wouldn't care if Motson had signed a deal with EA allowing it to use his likeness after his death.

"But in life or death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," Caufield said, adding that family members shouldn't "automatically" have the right to grant permission for AI recreations either.

At least one other game studio has taken a very different approach to the subject: Earlier this year, Darkest Dungeon developer Red Hook Studios said it would never use AI to recreate the voice of beloved narrator Wayne June, who died in 2025, despite having explicit permission from June himself to do so.

"I would never, ever erode his incredible and timeless performances by teaching a machine to sound like him," Red Hook co-founder Chris Bourassa remarked at the time.

The Japan Actors Union also recently began a push to protect the rights of voice actors with regard to AI, including a proposed ban on using AI to copy a dead actor's voice unless consent had been obtained prior to their death.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite a falling-out with the company that led to the creation of the PlayStation, former Sony Computer Entertainment CEO Ken Kutaragi notes he loves Nintendo.

For those unaware, Sony's first foray into the games industry was in collaboration with Nintendo, which was looking to create a CD-based add-on for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES) in the vein of the Sega CD. Sony and Nintendo's collaboration was dubbed the Play Station, but one day after Sony unveiled the collaboration, Nintendo confirmed a partnership with Philips to create a SNES CD. This led Sony to pursue its own console, with Kutaragi at the helm, resulting in the PlayStation, which sold over three times as many consoles as the N64.

Sources indicate that but despite the fallout, Kutaragi tells The Game Business, "I love Nintendo," adding, "I [contacted them] every week. One of my counterparts there was my best business friend. I love Nintendo games." He acknowledges the idea that PlayStation was made to get revenge on Nintendo, saying, "Many of the media said, 'Sony suffered a betrayal, they will take some revenge.' No. Totally no. We are all friends".

Recent findings suggest that kutaragi recalls just how much he worked with Nintendo – starting with a proposed disk for the NES, before working on the sound chip for the SNES itself – "I approached the Nintendo headquarters every week by using the bullet train. So, I seemed to be an acting member in Nintendo. [One woman there] assumed I was their employee. I had a very close relationship [with Nintendo].".

Ultimately, it probably worked out the best for everyone the way it did. Sony ended up making the most successful console ever with the PS2, and every one of its home consoles, barring the PS3, sold over 100 million units. Nintendo got a bit of a reality check when the N64 and GameCube didn't come close to Sony, and pivoted to unique hardware like the Wii and Switch. Shame about Sega though….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing new data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella mentioned on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active consumers] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

Breaking: GTA 6 vault: How to open them during substantial bank jobs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a big score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.
  • But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.
  • Here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a big score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.

But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.

Here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.

Your GTA 6 fence, Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun.

In a recent development, complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, and in Chapter 4 he'll offer you a tip for $10,000. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.

There are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!

You can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Massive Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City International Airport.

Follow the armored car until it parks outside a bank. Watch as one of the drivers gets out and walks into the bank. You can follow him to see where he goes, though bank layouts differ and he may take different routes. He may walk through the front doors, or he may go in a side entrance or a roll-up door in the back.

Once he's all the way inside—not just inside the front doors, but deep into the bank—he'll head to the vault and open it.

You can't open that vault yourself! Only the armored car driver can. That's the trick.

It has been revealed that once the guard is in the back of the bank, begin the robbery. Search for the vault in the back. You may need to use explosives to open the door the guard went through, or you can look for a door you can open with the snap gun. You'll find the vault door open with the armored car driver nearby. Subdue him and grab all the cash off the cart inside the vault.

There are several safe deposit boxes in the vault you can open for extra loot. Use your focus ability to highlight which boxes you can loot, and shoot them to open them up. You can also blow open all the boxes at once using a grenade or sticky bomb. Grab the loot from each.

If you really want to clean the place out, there's still all the cash drawers in the front of the bank and a small safe, or multiple safes, somewhere else, usually in an office in the back. You can open these standard safes with safe codes.

It has been revealed that the armored car parked outside has loot in it, too. The thing is, it may despawn while you're inside the bank. If you want to loot it, place a sticky explosive on the rear door, which won't let the truck despawn. (Be stealthy: there's another guard still watching the truck). When you leave the bank after the robbery, detonate the bomb and grab the loot.

The best way to enter a bank is through a back door, if the building has one, (using the snap gun to avoid alarms) or a roll-up door. If the guard you're following goes in the back, he may leave the doors unlocked behind him, and you may not even have to unlock any doors at all to reach the vault. Just be prepared to run into multiple security guards and employees you'll need to subdue.

According to recent reports, you will want both Jason and Lucia along for any bank vault jobs you pull. There is so much cash and valuables to grab you'll easily fill up four bags, which requires two people to carry. (You can hand loot bags to your partner by interacting with them and choosing the "Hand over bag" prompt). You'll also want one character to work as crowd control while you're looting the bank.

A silenced gun is a good idea: you want to delay setting off alarms for as long as possible, and if bank employees or citizens hear gunshots they may panic and trigger the alarm, or flee from the bank and call the cops.

It has been revealed that in a lot of robberies you can find the security footage and destroy it while the robbery is in progress. Big banks have cloud-based cameras which won't allow you to destroy the footage. Keep a lookout (using focus) for cameras and shoot them out (with silenced pistols) as quickly as you can.

If an alarm goes off during a vault robbery, you'll get an instant four-star wanted level, which means SWAT trucks, roadblocks, and helicopters. Park your car in a good spot outside so you can jump into it easily, and have some idea of where you want to drive to during your escape.

  • Recent findings suggest that nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being notable in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually.

GenAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it.".

Recent findings suggest that nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being notable in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually. And that seems to be changing fundamentally." He adds that maintaining a short gap also helps as, to put it simply, "people have short memories, right?" And, unfortunately, he's right; there are so many games coming out that adding something to your wishlist often feels like resigning it to remembering it exists six months later.

Recent findings suggest that he recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed. But then, he clarifies that the reason it seemed so easy was a lack of care. "There's a reason that every kind of AI slop game feels the same; it's because when you try to make something from zero, AI will multiply your skills, and zero times a thousand is still zero." The people claiming to 'develop' recomps do not care for making a game that feels right, or even one that works; they care only for the short-lived dopamine of being popular on Twitter for fifteen minutes before another slop copy rears its head (and is inevitably revealed to be jankware). Nichiporchik specifies that "game feel is impossible to copy; as long as you have a great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be okay." 'Game feel' is one of the vaguest terms that exists in this field, but I do feel that it refers to something tangible and immediately noticeable when it's gone.

Sources indicate that for example, I've recently been replaying the wonderful Celeste, and the 'game feel' of its wavedashing is core to making the practice of blazing through levels so engaging. The wavedash works the same every time, due to precise programming from Extremely OK Games spending time and effort painstakingly ensuring it did in the interest of consistency and unity in movement mechanics. You can't make good art without caring about the quality, even if there are now faster ways to knock together a 'working' game. To borrow an overused but still salient phrase: AI could never.

The music in question was tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6, which introduced on the same day (19th November). Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

Responding to the criticism, Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen noted he "woke up to a shit show".

"Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he wrote on X/Twitter, before inviting players to report complications and bugs to the email address shared in one of Nicalis' tweets, which confirmed it had "pushed a latest build with critical fixes", including the "removal of generated music files". The patch is live on PC, and Nicalis claims it has been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony.

Nicalis has yet to explain how the music ended up in the game.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence. Simultaneously, there's a certain something to The Witcher as a series that they feel is difficult to make tangible, but is something they want to ensure they don't lose sight of.

Weber describes the core of a 'Witcher-like' story to be something that "explores the various facets of human nature — a game for adults", which he clarifies doesn't just mean violence or sex, but "treating the player as a mature adult, asking difficult questions without offering easy answers." While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one.".

Of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri. Blacha explains that "Ciri isn't calm and composed like Geralt, nor does she hide her emotions easily. She is far more hot-headed and tends to be emotional when making decisions." In terms of how this actually affects the narrative itself and the protagonist's place in it, he elaborates that "when playing as Geralt, players acted more like an arbiter judging how to resolve a situation. When playing as Ciri, you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective." It's an interesting notion, to state that the difference in role is that where Geralt was more of a fixer, Ciri actually approaches situations on an interpersonal level. Weber seemingly half-jokes that "we find ourselves in a position very similar to Ciri's. Just as Ciri must succeed Geralt, we must create a game that lives up to The Witcher 3.".

As for how The Witcher 4 will play, moment to moment, Weber explains that some inspiration has been taken from Cyberpunk 2077 in regards to its open, player-led approach to customisation and, as a result, quests. "You could be a netrunner or a cyber ninja air-dashing into a scene with a double jump. We had to account for all those possibilities available to the player," he recalls. While I can't imagine Ciri will be air-dashing around Kovir, this statement does make me wonder how this approach can be applied to a game with such a specific existing protagonist, rather than the blank slate of Cyberpunk 2077's V. Recalling the side content of The Witcher 3 and its acclaim, he believes that people loved them "because we strived to offer something fresh" and "didn't create quests that merely waste the player's time", which is a principle that "remains unchanged today." Later, he condenses his feelings into the mantra that "A great quest can stem from a compelling story, an engaging character, or fantastic gameplay alone, but overall, there must be harmony.".

Towards the end of the interview, Blacha jokes that "One of our greatest achievements is convincing people to finish their workday, buy our game, and then clock into another job as a character inside the game." It's quite a long and engaging read, so if you're invested in The Witcher IV and its narrative development, I do encourage you read the entire thing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.
  • Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries noted. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves.".

Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

Industry observers note that "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe noted. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them.".

In a recent development, fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it.".

GTA 6 debuted on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

In a recent development, eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Robert Pattinson was just revealed as the next James Bond, and the internet has spent the days since joking that no Hollywood role is safe from him. I thought those jokes had about run their course until Ralph Fiennes weighed in. The actor who terrified an entire generation of Harry Potter fans as Lord Voldemort was asked who should take over the role in HBO's upcoming television series, and his answer was so dry that I almost missed how funny it was.

Fiennes was speaking with the Associated Press at the Upcoming York premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on Nov. 16. The conversation turned to the new book-to-screen adaptation of the Harry Potter novels and whether he'd consider returning as He Who Must Not Be Named. Fiennes indicated he'd had his fill of the character. As for who should put on the robes next, he offered one name:.

Maybe they'll offer it to Robert Pattinson.

I love how little effort went into that joke. The Red Dragon veteran actor didn't need to explain it, either. Following Pattinson's Bond casting, social media has been having a field day with the idea that he's taking every acting job. One popular variation suggests that artificial intelligence isn't coming for anyone's job because Pattinson will get there first. The OG Potter villain apparently decided to throw one more highly coveted part onto the pile.

Of course, there's another reason his suggestion is particularly good, and it involves a Harry Potter movie I still have a hard time watching without getting a little upset. Pattinson played Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, the same film that introduced Fiennes as the fully resurrected Voldemort. Cedric made it through the Triwizard Tournament only to be murdered by Peter Pettigrew on Voldemort's orders. It's a miserable ending for one of the story's most likable characters.

So imagine the actor who played Cedric now taking over as the man who ordered his death. I'd almost pay to see Pattinson in the makeup just for that bit of full-circle casting, although I'm pretty sure Fiennes was having a laugh rather than making a serious recommendation.

In a recent development, the two actors also have a second franchise connection thanks to Bond. Fiennes played M opposite Daniel Craig in Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die, so he's watched a different actor occupy the 007 role that Pattinson is now inheriting. The Tenet actor has already spent plenty of time bouncing between massive franchises, from Twilight to The Batman. It's getting hard to name an iconic fictional universe he hasn't visited.

Industry observers note that the actual casting of Voldemort remains a mystery. Fiennes previously remarked he was all for Cillian Murphy playing the Dark Lord, and there's been no shortage of rumors about who might portray the villain. He's also offered the eventual actor some practical advice on navigating Voldemort's robes. Whoever gets the job has quite a performance to follow.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I'm excited to see who HBO chooses, but Fiennes has made me realize there's one more possibility I hadn't considered. If Pattinson somehow lands the role, he'll have played Cedric Diggory and the wizard who had him killed. At this rate, I'd hesitate to rule out anything.

You can revisit Fiennes' take on Voldemort, or the eight films of the original Harry Potter film franchise, streaming with your HBO Max subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now confirmed that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a new, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:.

According to recent reports, "We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!".

The message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That said, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.
  • Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has a complicated control scheme that allows you to interact with the game in a variety of different ways. And while Rockstar does a good job introducing almost all of the title's mechanics, several useful features and commands are never mentioned at all. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you about some of its secret controls.

Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.

Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.

Double tap Triangle to get out of your car while the engine's still running:.

This can be useful for when you need to make a swift getaway, as you want waste time needing to start the engine.

One other quick tip here: if you're with a partner and need to rapidly get into the back seat, hold Triangle so your character doesn't waste time running around to the passenger side.

If the police know your identity but not necessarily your car, one way you can avoid being detected is by hiding behind the wheel.

Just park up somewhere discreet, and hold Circle to hide from any pursuing police:.

You can rest and lean on any surface by standing close to it and holding the Circle button, like shown:.

This can be useful if you're casing a joint, or just want to watch the world pass you by.

It has been revealed that you don't always need words to get your point across. There are situations where a middle finger will do.

Fortunately, GTA 6 has a solution for scenarios just like that.

While on foot, hold L2 and press R1 to give someone the finger:.

You can also do this while driving by simply pressing R1 while behind the wheel:.

Tapping Left and Right while driving will turn on your indicators, allowing you to signal to other motorists which way you're going:.

This can actually be useful when you're trying to drive safely, as oncoming cars will understand which way you're going and react accordingly. It can also help when you're merging lanes on motorways.

While more complex radio controls can be accessed by holding Left, did you know you can also quickly turn the radio on and off by double-tapping Left?

This works both in a car and when you're out and about using your earbuds.

If you press Square while driving, you can swiftly attack with your car door, as shown:.

This is really useful when you're being flanked by unsuspecting bikers — or you just want to show cyclists who's king the road!

Much like the above car door attack, you can kick any nearby enemies by pushing Square while you're riding a bike, as shown:.

This can help you knock rival motorcylists off their bike, or just give you a good core workout while on the highway.

You can go first-person at any time while you're on-foot and stationary by holding L2 and pressing R3:.

You can move the camera around from this position and press R2 to zoom, but you do need to hold L2 down throughout.

It's also worth noting you can't move while doing this, as there's no traditional first-person mode in the game.

This can be useful for reading signs and other looking closely at other objects in the game, though.

Every vehicle has a full suite of options you can access by holding Left and using the right analogue stick to navigate up to Vehicle, as shown:.

These options can include everything from winding down your windows to turning on your headlights. Speaking of which, you can also toggle your headlights at any time by pressing Circle:.

And, if you're in a boat, you can use the above vehicle management options to set down an anchor, which will keep it in place while you go diving:.

If you're playing on the PS5, the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers will help you observe the speed limit.

In a recent development, while you're driving, holding R2 until you feel the first point of resistance. This is the speed limit.

You'll need to have Adaptive Triggers Resistance enabled to feel this, and you can check it's on by pressing Options > Settings > Controller > DualSense Wireless Controller Features:.

You can take two cars when you're with your partner by using the command menu.

Hold Right to bring up the menu and press Cross/X to instruct your partner to drive:.

Then get in another car and hold Right again then press Square to follow you:.

You'll notice that your partner will drive right behind you, which can be useful if you need to setup getaway cars during robberies:.

In a recent development, did you know about any or all of these secret controls in GTA 6? You can find even more tips and tricks through the link, as well as tons of collectible and mission walkthroughs in our GTA 6 guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency.

Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings.

According to recent reports, on whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question.".

Blanche also remarked that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal.

"A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer remarked on Tuesday.

According to sources speaking to Reuters, Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, the latter of which is the firm associated with Alice Huang (no relation), the woman with whom Huang admitted to having an affair. (The CEO also reportedly had affairs with Nvidia employees.).

According to recent reports, in his return address to Nvidia staff, Huang said (via Marisa Kabas) that the tech giant's board opted to bring him back of their own accord, not because of pressure from the Trump administration. That statement is contradicted by Trump himself, who told CNBC that he "convinced" the Nvidia board to bring Huang back.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that nvidia's share price shot up following Huang's reinstatement, but dropped again by several points on Wednesday, and remains about 21.5% lower than it was at the start of this year. Trump is an Nvidia investor, and Nvidia donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom project.

Huang is scheduled to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

Sources indicate that tyler grew up in Silicon Valley during the '80s and '90s, playing games like Zork and Arkanoid on early PCs. He was later captivated by Myst, SimCity, Civilization, Command & Conquer, all the shooters they call "boomer shooters" now, and PS1 classic Bushido Blade (that's right: he had Bleem!). Tyler joined PC Gamer in 2011, and today he's focused on the site's news coverage. His hobbies include amateur boxing and adding to his 1,200-plus hours in Rocket League.

Industry observers note that if you want to enjoy your games, TV demonstrates and movies, getting a good-looking screen is half of the battle. OLED TVs are some of the best out there, due to the screen tech offering unmatched contrast and true darkness. Only, there's a catch.

Recent findings suggest that OLED TVs are some of the most expensive out there. That's why a Black Friday deal is helpful: it lets you pick up an expensive set at a greatly reduced cost. These sets are so expensive that discounts of hundreds, even thousands, of dollars are commonplace. In a recent development, if you're looking for a nice fresh gaming TV, you don't need OLED, of course. Your console or docked handheld will work just as well if you don't stretch for the premium tech.

According to recent reports, OLED is only to be seriously considered if you're putting some money towards a fancy home theater set-up, and want a great set to be part of that. OLED offers true blacks as the LEDs turn totally off, unlike on an LCD-based set, and the tech also offers more vivid colors, better contrast and wider viewing angles.

Industry observers note that some LCD technologies offer similar benefits at a lower price. Mini LED and QLED both use smaller backlights to offer great contrast in different ways, and some brands have their own technology to solve the LED shortcomings.

Screen tech isn't the only consideration too. If you're buying a set for gaming, you'll need to look into the number of ports and space behind the set, while screen size, operating system and mounting are all things to decide on before you buy a set.

Sources indicate that another day, another Steam enhancement! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

Industry observers note that for starters, there's a newly introduced Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in.".

In a recent development, next up in the revision is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

Industry observers note that there were a few other smaller bits to this update too. You'll find a new section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

Breaking: Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a latest patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat.
  • Recent findings suggest that the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November.
  • Industry observers note that the system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a latest patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat. The patent describes an AI-driven system that listens in on player voice chat following key gameplay moments and later recreates it using in-game characters.

Recent findings suggest that the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November. According to the filing and its diagrams, the system is a self-learning neural network that recognises major gameplay moments - such as kills, longshots, deaths and so on - and records the player's reaction and voice chat from the moment just before and then after they happen. These can be as simple as brief celebratory shouts, groans or yells, or as complex as trash talk.

Industry observers note that the system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions. The AI then teaches itself to swiftly identify those when they occur in-game and replicate them.

Although the replicated voice lines don't directly repeat players' own chat, the system does keep a profile of each player it analyses so it can deliver a response tailored to them, including sticking to the same spoken language, which it uses large language models (LLMs) to help identify. The patent describes a filter of sorts to keep NPCs from learning offensive language such as slurs.

According to the patent, the system's reach extends beyond in-game voice chat to also potentially access voice comms from major apps like Discord.

Activision's goal is to create NPCs that can speak naturally, rather than re-use the same pre-recorded lines. The application seems to be limited to multiplayer games, including those with co-op. Think of the generic voice lines spoken by AI-teammates like "cover me" and so on in a PvE game, or the many other similar ones in battle royale and PvP matches that contain dozens or hundreds of players.

Incidentally, the patent talks of replacing those generic messages with learned ones for players who join a match without a microphone, but players can also seemingly allow their in-game avatars to always use generated voices.

As the game industry continues to grapple with the use of generative-AI in game development, Activision's patent seems to be going directly to source, recreating how those LLMs and AI systems got their knowledge to begin with: from humans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most prominent figures of the so-called Bluenami was not a candidate on the ballot, but rather a Twitch streamer and political commentator: Hasan Piker.

This year Hasan was involved in dozens of races across the country, campaigning for progressive candidates like Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed. But you’re probably more likely to associate Hasan’s name with what other people have had to say about him—from Fox News commentators to more established members of the Democratic Party.

Hasan regularly courts controversy on both his hours-long Twitch streams, where he’s mentioned things like “America deserved 9/11,” and social media, where he’s written that Hamas “is a thousand times better than” Israel. He claims he’s often taken out of context, and that his audience knows what he really means—and where he stands. In his mind, he’s a leftist provocateur, maybe, but one who understands the importance of working-class values and electoral strategy.

While Hasan has walked back some of his more inflammatory language, his rhetoric raises the question: Is he a liability to the cause he champions? Or is he successfully reaching the critical audience—namely, young men—that helped elect the wave of progressives poised to take office in January?

With 2028 on the horizon, I wanted to know how Hasan thinks about his growing platform, and if he sees his role shifting in the media landscape. What responsibility does he have to his viewers and to the candidates he supports? And does he regret any of those past statements?

We also got into the DSA’s more extreme positions and how to make sense of them; why he thinks the Republicans put his thirst trap on the jumbotron at their convention; and how he, a self-proclaimed socialist, thinks about his own money.

According to recent reports, okay. We’ll take the compliment.

But the serious answer is, I mean, I reach an audience that obviously does not watch television, does not read legacy publications at all. And I want to show people that read Vanity Fair that I am not a terrorist.

Sources indicate that yeah, exactly. That would be the name of the episode. I’ll do interviews with candidates. I’ll go out and—.
